steps.purpose: Use one actual cleanup deadline across test body, helpers and pytest fixture finalizers.
steps.target: New H2 protocol watchdogs and common PG fixture integration only; historical normal/H1 watchdogs unchanged.
steps.method: Each new protocol hook temporarily installs its controller on item.config under a private test-only attribute, restoring prior value in finally. Controller exposes cleanup_remaining(maximum), which idempotently begins its existing cleanup clock and returns strictly positive remaining seconds without extending it. No second timer, fresh cleanup epoch or environment switch. Common fixture receives pytest request/config and consults this optional controller; absence preserves legacy limits. Controller stays installed through pytest_runtest_teardown(nextitem=None), which calls teardown_exact(None) and includes session fixture finalizers. It is restored only after the whole protocol. pytest_sessionfinish may perform abnormal remaining cleanup outside a case; such a path cannot count as passing per-case cleanup and needs outer runner proof.
steps.agent: Code-dev integration; TC literal watchdog/fixture oracles.
steps.pass_criteria: Same monotonic epoch governs every helper and finalizer; SQL25+5 and integration215+25 remain unchanged; timer/handler/config restoration happens even on evidence errors. A remaining-time failure is a failed case with parent-runner owned cleanup, never a pass or claimed absence.
steps.expected: Per-case cleanup cannot silently consume15+5+25 seconds under a25s cap.
steps.evidence: Exact plugin/fixture source diffs and hashes, reviewed whole-case timing, private lifecycle; final actual full gate.
steps.recovery: Preserve original error and owned identities; outer runner reaps only its descendants, records cleanup failure; fix relevant helper and refreeze complete gate.

steps.purpose: Close every resource in the H2 fixture dependency closure under the same cleanup clock, not just PG stop.
steps.method: Propagate optional request.config controller to these test-only finalizers. DB DROP opens with a bounded connection allowance only if sufficient budget remains, then sets lock_timeout and statement_timeout using remaining milliseconds; no unbounded DROP. HBA restore uses existing file bytes then pinned pg_ctl reload with remaining subprocess timeout. OIDC close uses a single absolute deadline for all owned servers/threads, requests shutdown concurrently or otherwise bounds each blocking call, checks every thread stopped and retains handles on failure; no per-thread fresh3s budgets. TestClient contexts must quiesce maintenance deterministically during fixture setup using their existing test portal (cancel/await the actual app.state.maintenance_task) for H2 cases, recording completion before body; this does not change production app behavior. Context exit still runs actual lifespan finalization; bound teardown/portal exit under the same case clock and fail if unconfirmed. Do not detach a live thread and label it stopped. Existing no-controller fixture behavior stays unchanged.
steps.agent: Code-dev shared fixture integration; TC resource/timing/failure oracles.
steps.pass_criteria: All function and last-item session finalizers are within one clock; no native DB, subprocess, thread or TestClient wait can silently outlive it on a passing case. All owned resources have affirmative termination evidence. Connection/SQL/server/thread uncertainty is failure; retain handles and leave only bounded outer runner cleanup after failure. Original auth tests still exercise production maintenance; H2 quiescence is explicit fixture-specific exception with privacy/auth preservation regression.

steps.recovery: Retain primary error plus cleanup/resource status. Parent subreaper terminates only its owned child process tree on failed/unresponsive pytest; refreeze all impacted fixtures and full407+all25 gate after correction.

steps.purpose: Bound PG stop within the remaining shared case budget and observe the current postmaster after restart.
steps.target: tests/ifpmic_api/conftest.py PG lifecycle cleanup and private lifecycle metadata.
steps.method: Before stop, read the owned private data-directory postmaster.pid and capture current PID/start ticks, including restarted instance. Signal only through pinned pg_ctl for that exact private directory. Under active H2 controller allocate short fast-stop, immediate fallback and status-check timeouts from remaining budget, reserving time for fallback; no individual subprocess gets the old25s allowance after other cleanup. Preserve legacy path if no active controller. Persist initial and current identities and absence check; do not report stopped merely because original pre-restart PID disappeared. No OS-wide kill or service restart during cleanup.
steps.agent: Code-dev integration; TC PG restart and timeout/failure oracles.
steps.pass_criteria: Current saved identity is absent after actual stop; original and restarted identities retained privately. Every timeout/fallback/status call obeys the same absolute cleanup cap. steps.recovery: Retain private postmaster/storage/journal evidence, fail case, stop only owned storage/PID through bounded parent cleanup, diagnose and rerun exact full candidate.
